tagline: Across the reservation, over Satus Pass, down to the Columbia.
intro: The designated byway follows US 97 south from Union Gap, but the road drawn here starts at Fort Simcoe, in the foothills of the Cascades, and comes east through White Swan to Toppenish, a farm town that lies entirely within the Yakama Reservation. There it turns south on US 97, leaves the farmland behind and climbs slowly into the hills toward the Simcoe Mountains and over Satus Pass, 3,107 feet up.

On the far side it drops through Goldendale to the Columbia near Maryhill, where Sam Hill's unfinished mansion was dedicated as a museum by the Queen of Romania. The byway is spelled for the Yakama people, not the city of Yakima.

moments.title: Fort Simcoe
moments.text: The army built its post here in the late 1850s, in an old oak grove watered by springs, used it only three years, and five of the original buildings still stand.

moments.title: Toppenish
moments.text: The first mural, "Clearing the Land", went up in 1989, and more than 75 now cover the town's walls, every one set somewhere between 1840 and 1940.

moments.title: Goldendale
moments.text: The telescope on the hill north of town was built by four amateurs for a Vancouver college that wanted clearer, darker skies, until a Goldendale diner owner suggested they give it to the town.
